lens: accuracy and fairness: every statement and on-screen text checked against research/claims.json and quotes.json
method: I dumped every narration line, spoken override and on-screen text item from all 15 chapters with each shot's cited claims (213 distinct ids; all exist; every narrated shot cites at least one). I machine-matched all 79 quoted fragments (spoken and on screen) against quotes.json: all are verbatim, and I checked each speaker, date and context against its entry. The only quoted string that did not match is the mentioned word 'rabbit' (L1504), which is not a quotation. I read every remaining line and label against the claims its shot cites, with the bible (people list, era analyses, AlexNet/Transformer primers, Era 13 belief sequence, contested-matters section) as backup. I also checked the visuals where staging carries facts (ch03-s01, ch05-s04, ch06-s04, ch08-s05, ch10-s11, ch13-s06, ch14-s07, ch15-s05, ch15-s08). Round 2's two critical items are fixed: DeepMind is now credited for AlphaGo, Chinchilla and AlphaFold, and the BIS rationale for the export controls is quoted beside Beijing's reply. Most of round 2's issues were also fixed (Turing's 3 in 10, 'over one in four', the Turing Award scoping, the DAIR context, the METR caveat, the toy-stencil tag, the Vapnik and Kai Li credits, 'most of thirty-six years', the Hinton name card at the phone call, GOOGLE · 2016, the XOR demo readout, and the runtime trim to 3,179 words).
critical: BRIEF GAP: TALENT IS MISSING FROM THE US–CHINA RACE (ch14). The brief's guardrail names five strands: export controls, compute, talent, open-weight models and safety debates. Talent never appears in narration or on screen. Open weights get only 'open to all' (L1408) and a Qwen name card. The research has verified material: e13-talent (MacroPolo: of top NeurIPS 2022 authors, 47% did their undergraduate degree in China, against 18% in the US, yet the US remained the leading place they worked) and e13-qwen / e13-open-releases (Qwen passed Llama in cumulative Hugging Face downloads by October 2025). FIX: in ch14-s04 after L1410, or in ch14-s07 before L1417, add about 25 words: 'And the people? Of the top researchers at one big conference, nearly half had first studied in China. Most still worked in America.' Add the label 'NeurIPS 2022 top authors · undergraduate degree: China 47% · US 18% · most work in the US (MacroPolo)'. Optionally add one label on the open-weights strand: 'Oct 2025 · Alibaba's open Qwen passes Meta's Llama in downloads (Hugging Face data)'. Cite e13-talent and e13-qwen.

CONTESTED CREDIT STATED AS FACT, ch15-s06 L1509: 'The three who kept these networks alive through the winters lived to see them win'. This is the 'Fathers of the Deep Learning Revolution' framing. The bible says to attribute it as ACM's own framing because it is contested by people who stress Schmidhuber's group, Fukushima, Amari and Ivakhnenko (e9-turing). The film's own earlier chapters credit Amari, Linnainmaa, Fukushima, Hochreiter and Schmidhuber, and IDSIA, so the closing line contradicts the film's even-handedness at its most memorable moment. FIX: 'Three of those who kept these networks alive through the winters lived to see them win; now two warn this road is dangerous, the third that it doesn't go far enough.' (one added word, 'of those').

A REAL PERSON'S WORD USED ON THE WRONG QUESTION, ch14-s07 L1421: 'Nanoseconds, says a chip seller.' The line answers 'how wide is the AI gap', but Jensen Huang said China was 'nanoseconds behind' in CHIPS (e13-gap, BG2, 26 September 2025), and the bible notes he said it 'while arguing for sales'. Lifting his word into the model-gap question puts a claim in his mouth that he did not make. FIX: 'Nanoseconds behind, in chips, says a chip seller.' Also extend the name card: 'Jensen Huang · Nvidia, chip seller · on chips · Sept 2025'.

issues.problem: The Hugging Face breach is narrated as 'test agents broke out of their sandbox'. The narration leaves out what e14-hf-incident establishes: this was a deliberate cyber-attack evaluation (ExploitGym), run with reduced cyber refusals and without production safeguards. Only the open-valve prop in the visual hints at this, and no viewer will read it that way. The round-2 outside-expert framing ('with the safeties turned off') has been cut. As written, an evaluation failure sounds like a rogue escape in normal use, which is unfair to OpenAI next to Anthropic's sympathetically framed refusal.
issues.fix: 'In a hacking test, with safeguards deliberately lowered, OpenAI's agents broke out of their sandbox into Hugging Face, hunting their own test's answers; OpenAI called it a warning shot.' (+8 words). Alternatively, set the date stamp to 'OPENAI · HUGGING FACE · A HACKING TEST, SAFEGUARDS LOWERED · 9–13 JULY 2026 · DISCLOSED 21 JULY'.

issues.problem: Only Anthropic's side of the Pentagon dispute is given: what it refused, after which the Pentagon 'branded it'. The bible's contested-matters entry states the government's position ('a contractor imposing use limits is a supply-chain risk; the D.C. Circuit majority found motive irrelevant'). Round 2 credited the script with including the government's side, but that side is no longer spoken or shown. The verb 'branded' also leans toward Anthropic.
issues.fix: 'Anthropic would not drop its limits on mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons. The Pentagon, saying a supplier may not set such limits, named it a supply-chain risk. Courts are split.' Optionally add a small label under the court label: '“completely validates the Department's position” — Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell, 25 Sep 2026' (q14-parnell).

issues.problem: 'Then three great halls ... and a thousand doors' counts four fully connected stages, but AlexNet has three: fc6 (4096), fc7 (4096) and fc8, which is the 1,000-way output (e8-architecture). The shot's own label reads '4096 · 4096 · 1000'. The line also conflicts with ch08-s08b's label 'the two big halls only (fc6, fc7)'. The visual stacks three halls and then a crown of doors, which repeats the error.
issues.fix: 'Then two great halls, where every lantern sees everything, and a last hall of a thousand doors, one per answer.' Visual: two halls, then the doors as the third fully connected layer.

issues.problem: 'Nobody told the towers to divide the work.' The two-GPU split was designed in: half the kernels on each card, communicating only at certain layers (e8-gpu-split). What nobody told them was HOW to divide it, which is the actual finding (colour-agnostic on one card, colour-specific on the other).
issues.fix: 'Nobody told the towers how to divide the work. One learned black and white, one colour. Every time.'

issues.problem: The shot depicts the holdouts of the 'fiddly nets' era and the 2004 NCAP thread, and LeCun's quote is from the NCAP context. The bible's people list has LeCun at Bell Labs from 1988 and NYU from 2003, and its era analysis says 'Bell Labs, then NYU'. The visual's own stamp says 'HOLMDEL / NEW YORK'. The card is out of date for most of the era shown.
issues.fix: 'Yann LeCun · Bell Labs, then NYU'.

issues.problem: This was carried over from round 2 and is still unfixed. The image is the Mark I's motorised knob, whose build date is contested (e2-mark1-build: assembled 1958–59, first shown publicly 23 June 1960). ch03-s04, ch06-s01 and ch08-s03 now say '1958–60', so the finale disagrees with the rest of the film.

'It became ImageNet: over a million photos, a thousand categories, a yearly contest.' ImageNet itself had about 11 million images in 15,000+ categories by April 2010 (e7-imagenet-19years). The 1.2 million photos and 1,000 categories describe the contest subset (e7-ilsvrc2010), which the shot's label correctly calls 'IMAGENET CHALLENGE'.
issues.fix: 'It became ImageNet, and from it a yearly contest: over a million photos, a thousand categories.'

issues.problem: 'Almost nobody could teach a middle layer. Then someone wrote a book about why.' Perceptrons proved what single-layer, order-limited perceptrons cannot compute (e3-perceptrons). It explained nothing about why hidden layers could not be trained, and offered only an 'intuitive judgment' about them (e3-sterile), as ch04-s02 itself says. The bridge line misstates the book's content.
issues.fix: 'Almost nobody could teach a middle layer. Then two men wrote a book about what one layer could never do.'

issues.where: ch07-s02 nameCard 'Geoffrey Hinton, University of Toronto' / L0703
issues.problem: The narration says 'they wrote', and the quote card is attributed 'Hinton & Salakhutdinov', but only Hinton gets a name card. The co-author of the Science paper (e7-autoencoder) is never named, and neither are Osindero and Teh of the 2006 deep-belief-net paper (e7-dbn).
issues.fix: Name card: 'Geoffrey Hinton · Ruslan Salakhutdinov · Toronto' (optionally add 'with Simon Osindero, Yee-Whye Teh: deep belief nets, 2006').

issues.problem: 'Eight names, in random order', yet only Llion Jones gets a name card. Vaswani and Shazeer never appear by name in the film, although the footnote credits Shazeer with proposing scaled dot-product and multi-head attention (e10-author-order), the very mechanics ch10-s06 to ch10-s08 teach. A fairness gap on credit, in the chapter about credit being shared.
issues.fix: On the 'random' beat, letter the eight shuffling slips with the eight surnames (Vaswani · Shazeer · Parmar · Uszkoreit · Jones · Gomez · Kaiser · Polosukhin, from e10-arxiv), as one text item. Keep the Jones card for the title beat.

issues.problem: The DAIR card now says 'on the AI pause letter', but the film never introduces the pause letter (e12-fli is cited in ch13-s04 and never shown). Viewers meet a reply to a letter they never heard of. The bible also notes that 'no major lab paused' and that Bengio signed it.
issues.fix: In ch13-s03 before L1308, add: 'In March, an open letter asked labs to pause for six months. None did.' (12 words). Or add a label on the strip beat: 'March 2023 · open letter: pause training beyond GPT-4 for 6 months · no major lab paused'.

issues.problem: The even-handed 'cooperation alongside competition' strand (bible Era 13-E) is carried only by an unlabelled visual page 'BLETCHLEY 2023' and the 2026 dialogue. e12-bletchley (the US and China both signed) is cited in ch13-s06 and ch14-s07 but never spoken. The research also notes that chip controls were unchanged at the 2026 summit (e13-summits-2026), which keeps the cooperation line from overstating the thaw.
issues.fix: 'Yet the two shores had signed the same safety declaration at Bletchley in 2023, and this September agreed an AI dialogue and an incident channel, with the chip rules unchanged.'

issues.where: ch10-s12 OST '12 hours · one machine, 8 chips · ≈ 1/7 the compute'
issues.problem: '≈ 1/7 the compute' (and 'the old compute' in L1025) gives no baseline. The ratio is specifically base Transformer versus Google's GNMT+RL, and it is derived (e10-flops).
issues.fix: '≈ 1/7 the compute of Google's previous translator (GNMT+RL; derived from the paper's estimates)'.

issues.where: ch15-s02 OST 'January 2025 · DeepSeek-R1, method published · reasoning stage ≈ $294,000'
issues.problem: The $294,000 figure was disclosed in Nature on 17 September 2025, not in January, and it excludes about $6 million for the base model (e14-r1). Under a January date it reads as a January claim of the whole cost.
issues.fix: 'January 2025 · DeepSeek-R1, method published · reasoning stage ≈ $294,000, on top of the ≈ $6M base model (disclosed Sept 2025)'.

issues.problem: This card sits under 'What use was it?' with no context, so it reads as Rosenblatt's answer to that question. The New Yorker reports it as his answer to what the perceptron was NOT capable of (q-rosenblatt-love context).
issues.fix: Attribution: '— Frank Rosenblatt, asked what it could never do, The New Yorker, 6 December 1958'.

issues.problem: 'blame(hidden i) = Σ_j blame(j) · w_ji' leaves out the hidden unit's own slope. In Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams (e4-rhw), the blame on a unit's input is the summed blame from above times the derivative of its activation, y_i(1 − y_i). As written, the equation is inconsistent with the Δw line that uses the same 'blame'. Only a careful viewer would catch it, but the film promises real mechanics.
issues.fix: 'blame(i) = slope(i) · Σ_j blame(j) · w_ji     Δw_ji = −ε · blame(j) · y_i', or add a small tag: 'slope term omitted'.

issues.problem: The tube count is contested (e1-snarc-tubes: Minsky recalled about 300; the AIMA textbook says 3,000). The card states Minsky's figure without attribution.
issues.fix: 'SNARC · about 40 "neurons" · about 300 tubes (Minsky's recollection)'.

issues.problem: 'Then the field got a name' lands under the 1956 stamp, but the term was introduced in the proposal dated 31 August 1955 (e1-dartmouth-proposal).
issues.fix: Put 'named in the proposal, August 1955' in the 'ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE' label, or move the name beat before the 1956 stamp.

issues.problem: 'It also paid one and a half billion over pirated books.' The record shows a $1.5 billion class settlement with final approval on 20 July 2026 (e14-copyright). It does not show that payment was made. The research also records the same judge's ruling that training on lawfully bought books was fair use, so the line tells half the legal outcome.
issues.fix: 'It also agreed to pay one and a half billion over pirated books.' (Optional, for balance: 'training on bought books, the judge said, was fair use.')

issues.where: ch13-s02 OST / L1304 'Google has acted very responsibly.'
issues.problem: quotes.json still marks q12-hinton-tweet as secondary (Wikipedia) and says to check the original tweet before using it as on-screen text. The attribution now says 'as widely reproduced', which is honest, but the tweet itself has not been verified.
issues.fix: Have research confirm the fragment against the original tweet (or an archive) and update the quote entry. If it cannot be confirmed, keep the current attribution.

issues.problem: These lines speak 'AI' as bare capitals with no spoken override, while L0515, L0522 and L0909 use 'A.I.'. TTS may read 'AI' as a word ('eye'), and the narrator would pronounce it inconsistently across the film.
issues.fix: Add spoken overrides with 'A.I.' to all four lines (inside quotations too, since spoken overrides do not change on-screen text), or confirm that the narration lexicon maps 'AI' to 'A.I.'.

strengths: Quote discipline is exemplary. All 79 quoted fragments, spoken and on screen, match quotes.json word for word, with correct speakers, dates and provenance ('as quoted by Gary Marcus', 'AP translation', 'as reported by Cade Metz', 'as widely reproduced', 'recalling colleagues' advice'). Spoken quotes are trimmed at clause boundaries without changing their sense, and paraphrases (Fei-Fei Li's colleagues, Huang's apart) carry no quote marks.

Round 2's lab-balance fix landed well. DeepMind is now named on AlphaGo (narration and card), Chinchilla, the Hoffmann quote, the Hassabis 'six months' tag and the AlphaFold chemistry prize, with Baker's half credited. OpenAI's founding names Altman, Musk and Sutskever. 'Two labs, under the same light' no longer promises more than it delivers. Anthropic's own study is labelled as its own and carries its 'about a quarter of the prompts' limitation, and the closing disclosure states the film's own provenance.

The US–China material is now properly two-sided at its core. Washington's stated rationale is quoted verbatim (BIS, 7 October 2022) beside Beijing's verbatim reply. China's 2017 plan 'named no rival'. DeepSeek's $5.6 million carries both the report's own caveat and the outside SemiAnalysis estimate. The gap candle is labelled contested and ends on 'nobody agrees'. The September 2026 dialogue and incident channel sit beside the competition.

Contested facts are marked as contested throughout: the bedroom-or-lab account of AlexNet's training, the Mark I's 1958–60 build, backprop priority ('credit still disputed', with Linnainmaa and Amari acknowledged), Gebru's departure (both accounts on screen, same size), the auction details 'by one reporter's account' with 'terms never disclosed', the warm-up candle 'nobody knows exactly when', systematicity 'still argued', and the expert-systems candle dated to the boom, with 'rule engines lived on'.

The deep-dive arithmetic is right and checkable. 224 × 224 × 3 = 150,528. The Sobel cell comes to 3.88. 32² × 2 = 2,048 crops. log₂1000 ≈ 10 bits against 60 million weights. Dropout applies to fc6/fc7 only. ReLU's 6× is scoped to the 4-layer CIFAR-10 test net. The 15.3% is a seven-net ensemble, two of them pre-trained, with the best single net at 18.2% on validation. Scores 2,0,4,2 ÷ √4 → 1,0,2,1 give a softmax share of about 0.53 to 'river'. √64 = 8, 8 heads × 64, × 6 layers, 12 hours on 8 P100s, and n² cost.

The candle clock is faithful to the bible's era analysis: 1943–1959 (16), the perceptron's about 7 years, sterile 1969–1986 (17), the knowledge boom c. 1980–1987, hand features c. 1999–2012 (13), read-in-order 20 years, Kaplan's recipe 2 years, one-to-three-years-behind about 2 years, and the 27 January 2025 market belief at a single day. Every candle still burning is tagged 'contested, as of October 2026'.

Every death, illness and grief beat is handled with restraint and is sourced: Pitts and McCulloch in 1969, Rosenblatt's 43rd birthday and the 1972 dedication, Lenat in 2023, Widrow at 95, and the closing of Mechanical Turk. The dissenters (Gerard, Minsky in 1961, Lighthill, Fodor and Pylyshyn, Vapnik's bet, Bender and Koller, Gebru, Marcus, LeCun) are each given their strongest verified words, never caricatured.
